notes:
Promptline gets a second theme, Indigo, and from here on a new theme every month. Builds on [v0.2.17](https://github.com/bekalpaslan/promptline/releases/tag/v0.2.17).

### Themes

- **Indigo, the first monthly theme.** **Settings → Appearance → Theme** now offers **Instrument**, the look you have today, and **Indigo**: a near-black ground, indigo as the one accent, rounder controls and cards, tag chips with an edge, and the popup's search as a pill. Every theme has a light and a dark side, so the **System / Light / Dark** control is now called **Mode** and works as before. A new theme joins the list every month; this is the first.
- **Nothing changes until you pick it.** An upgraded install stays on Instrument, which looks exactly as it did in 0.2.17.
- **config.json gains a `palette` field** that records the theme. An older version reading the file ignores it; nothing else on disk moves.
- **Inter joins the Font list**, beside the system font, Outfit, serif and mono. A theme never changes the font, so the two choices are separate.

### Hotkey

- **An upgrade keeps its hotkey even when the first launch goes wrong.** 0.2.17 promised that an install from 0.2.16 or earlier keeps `Ctrl+Shift+V`, but that held only when every step of startup succeeded: a locked or read-only config.json, or a data-folder move that failed, could leave the install on `Ctrl+Alt+V`. Now any doubt counts as an existing install, and a launch that can't record the hotkey registers the one you have and tries again next time.
- **Settings never names a hotkey the install doesn't have.** While the configuration loads, or when the library fails to load, the first-run banner, the gear's tooltip and Settings say nothing about a specific combination, instead of showing `Ctrl+Alt+V` on an install that registered something else.

### Security

- **Buy me a coffee is the only link the app will open.** The command behind that button used to pass any https address from the window to the shell; it now opens only that one listed address and refuses everything else. Nothing changes in what the app sends over the network.
